action-pinning.description: The actions CI uses are pinned to full commit SHAs

ci-build-types.description: CI builds Debug and Release, with and without sanitizers, everywhere

ci-current.description: Every CI configuration is in use, none left from a CI the project moved away from

ci-lint.description: CI lints its own configuration (e.g. actionlint or zizmor)

ci-present.description: The project has continuous integration configured

code-formatting.description: Formatting is defined (e.g. .clang-format, ruff, rustfmt) and CI enforces it

committed-artifacts.description: No build outputs (e.g. object files, __pycache__/, target/) are committed

compile-commands.description: compile_commands.json is exported (CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS; Meson always writes it)

compiler-extensions.description: Compiler extensions are disabled (-std=c++NN or -std=cNN rather than -std=gnu++NN or -std=gnuNN)

compiler-warnings.description: A strict compiler warning (or lint) set is enabled

copy-paste-detection.description: CI runs copy-paste detection (e.g. PMD CPD or jscpd)

coverage.description: CI measures branch coverage (or the finest the language's tools measure), reports it where it can be seen and fails under a threshold; path coverage is a bonus

data-wellformed.description: Every data file is well formed: it parses in its format (JSON, TOML, YAML and XML are built in)

dependency-audit.description: CI checks the dependencies against known vulnerabilities (e.g. pip-audit, cargo audit, govulncheck)

dependency-management.description: Dependencies come from a package manager (CPM, vcpkg, uv, Cargo) and are locked, not vendored

dependency-updates.description: Automated dependency updates are configured (Dependabot, Renovate or Scala Steward)

file-soundness.description: CI checks the project's binary and asset files (e.g. ClamAV, magick, qpdf)

function-limits.description: Function length is limited (lizard, or each language's linter rule)

fuzz-testing.description: Fuzz targets exist (e.g. libFuzzer, cargo-fuzz, atheris, Go fuzzing) and CI runs them

large-files.description: Large files are stored with Git LFS or DVC rather than committed directly

license.description: The project has a license file of a known license

link-check.description: CI checks each documentation site's links in each unit and fails on a broken one (lychee, sphinx-build -b linkcheck, markdown-link-check, mdbook-linkcheck, linkinator, muffet, htmltest, HTMLProofer); a scheduled run counts. Warns otherwise

migration-safety.description: CI checks each language's database migrations in each unit for changes that are unsafe to apply to a live database (squawk, atlas migrate lint, liquibase checks run). Warns otherwise; a project without migrations is not judged

mutation-testing.description: CI runs mutation testing (e.g. mutmut, cargo-mutants, StrykerJS, PIT), ideally on a pull request's changes only

out-of-source-build.description: The build prevents in-source builds (CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR compared with CMAKE_BINARY_DIR; Meson always does)

platform-matrix.description: CI runs on several operating systems with several compilers (or interpreter/toolchain versions)

repository-hygiene.description: No Trojan Source characters, conflict markers, unportable paths, broken links or stray LFS pointers

sanitizers.description: Sanitizers are used in some configuration: AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer for C and C++ (one of the two warns), cargo miri test or -Zsanitizer for Rust, go test -race for Go

schema-compatibility.description: CI checks each format's schemas in each unit for breaking changes against the main branch or a registry (buf breaking, oasdiff breaking, json-schema-diff)

schema-declared.description: Every schema declares its dialect and its identifier ($schema and $id, an openapi version and info.version, a targetNamespace, a syntax and package); a superseded dialect warns

schema-examples.description: CI checks the examples that come with each format's schemas in each unit: valid ones that must pass and invalid ones that must fail (ajv test, a validator run on examples/, spectral, schemathesis)

schema-validation.description: CI validates each format's documents in each unit against their schemas (check-jsonschema, ajv, kubeconform, helm lint --strict)

secret-scanning.description: CI scans for committed secrets (e.g. gitleaks, TruffleHog)

security-policy.description: A security policy says how to report a vulnerability privately

security-scanning.description: CI scans the code for security problems (CodeQL, GitLab SAST, or each language's security lints)

static-analysis.description: Static analyzers are configured and run (e.g. clang-tidy and cppcheck, ruff check, clippy)

status-badges.description: The README shows CI status and code quality badges

tests-run.description: Tests exist (registered with CTest or Meson for C and C++) and CI runs them

top-level-guard.description: Tests and developer-only settings are guarded by PROJECT_IS_TOP_LEVEL (Meson: meson.is_subproject()), so the project works as a subproject

type-checking.description: CI runs a static type checker on dynamically typed code (e.g. mypy, pyright), ideally strictly

vcs-ignore.description: A .gitignore (or .hgignore, .bzrignore, ...) keeps build outputs (e.g. build/, __pycache__/, target/) out of version control

warnings-as-errors.description: Compiler warnings are treated as errors in at least one configuration
